title: Demonstratives and αὐτός
description: The demonstratives οὗτος (this) and ἐκεῖνος (that), and the two further uses of αὐτός: "self" and "same".

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html: οὗτος and ἐκεῖνος stand in the predicate position: the article goes with the noun and the demonstrative stands outside it, before or after (οὗτος ὁ ἀπόστολος or ὁ ἀπόστολος οὗτος, this apostle). Used alone they mean this man, that woman, these things. αὐτός has three uses: in the oblique cases it is the pronoun him, her, it (Unit 8); in the predicate position it means self (αὐτὸς ὁ ἀπόστολος, the apostle himself); in the attributive position it means same (ὁ αὐτὸς ἀπόστολος, the same apostle).

blocks.caption: οὗτος, this
rows: The rough breathing and τ go together with the article: where the article has a rough breathing (ὁ, ἡ, οἱ, αἱ) οὗτος has one too; elsewhere it begins with τ. The stem vowel is ου where the ending has ο or ω, and αυ where it has α or η.

blocks.caption: ἐκεῖνος, that
blocks.html: ἐκεῖνος, ἐκείνη, ἐκεῖνο is declined like αὐτός: neuter singular in -ο, otherwise like ἀγαθός.

blocks.caption: Common confusion
blocks.html: αὕτη (this woman, rough breathing, accent on the first syllable) and αὐτή (she, smooth breathing, accent on the last) differ only in breathing and accent. αὐτὸς ὁ κύριος is the Lord himself; ὁ αὐτὸς κύριος is the same Lord.
